text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Cooperation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Police investigators say the murder on Sunday of leading businessman Valery Michugin and his girlfriend, Natalija Meisane, who died in hospital, could have been caused either either by jealousy or business rivalry.
- The government has submitted its deficit-free budget draft to parliament and it has been sent to the parliamentary committees concerned.
- 10 MPs have asked explanations from the ministry of the interior and ministry of justice about the release by police of Alexandrs Petersons, accused of the sexual abuse of children.

- The National TV and Radio Council considered yesterday the request by four Latvian TV companies to annul the licence of the Latvian Independent TV. Lawyers dismissed allegations that the company is violating the law.

- Former interior minister Janis Adamsons announced that on Thursday he will decide whether to stay in his party, Latvia's Way, or leave it. The party is one of the leading groups in the government coalition.

- President Guntis Ulmanis and Prime Minister Andris Shkele will speak before the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe and a session of the U.N. in New York, respectively. The president's speech will focus on the state of human rights and the situation of national minorities in Latvia.
- Explosions hit three Vision Express shops in the Lithuanian capital, second city Kaunas and the northern town of Panvezhys.
